title: API contract resilience framework for behavior-flag sunset and streaming/tool-call deprecations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Establish a repeatable framework and automated harness to safely sunset behavior flags and related API surface changes affecting streaming responses, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. Deliverables: (1) compatibility validator that runs shadow requests against new behavior(s), (2) streaming replayer for token-level regression detection, (3) schema verifier for tool-call payloads and structured-output parsers, (4) migration hints surfaced via SDK/console, and (5) telemetry and alerting to catch customer regressions during rollouts.
decision_record: Choice: Prefer shadow-run + lightweight replay over immediate toggled rollout to reduce customer-visible regressions.
Tradeoff: Shadow-run increases compute cost (approx +7%) but dramatically reduces rollbacks and support burden.
Choice: Use deterministic replayer for streaming to compare token sequences and a fuzz-tolerant diff for structured outputs (JSON schema + semantic key checks).
Tradeoff: Strict byte-for-byte comparison is too brittle for paraphrases; we will expose a configurable tolerance level per test suite.

acceptance_criteria: Compatibility harness runs in CI and produces a human-readable report for each candidate change.
Streaming replayer reproduces past N=1000 streaming sessions deterministically and flags token divergence > configured threshold.
Tool-call schema verifier rejects incompatible shape changes in PRs unless an explicit migration note is present.
Console surfaces per-customer migration hints when a flagged behavior will change (link to migration guide).
Rollout automation can perform a canary (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automatically pause on defined regression signals.
test_plan: Unit: parsers, schema verifier, streaming-diff utils (CI).
Integration: shadow-run on staging with recorded traffic from last 2 weeks (anon) and automated report generation.
Regression: run streaming replayer against golden set (1000 sessions) and verify no regression above tolerance.
E2E: deploy canary with 1% traffic, exercise critical SDK flows (chat streaming, tool call, structured-output parsing) and validate telemetry.
Chaos: simulate node restart and KV cache warm vs cold to validate fallback behavior during rollout.

rollout_plan: Phase 0: CI/Canary - run compatibility harness in CI for every relevant PR (blocking for runtime changes).
Phase 1: Shadow-run on staging with live traffic (no customer exposure) for 7 days and fix top-3 regressions.
Phase 2: Canary 1% production traffic for 48 hours with accelerated telemetry (1s granularity), pause on regressions.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% over one week with automatic rollback on regression triggers.
Phase 4: Full rollout and mark old behavior-flag deprecated; schedule flag removal in 90 days if no high-severity regressions.
rollback_criteria: Customer-visible errors spike by >5% in the affected flows (chat streaming or tool-call).
Token-level divergence above configured threshold in >0.5% of sessions for >30 minutes.
Critical customer report triage indicates loss of structured-output interpretability for a paying customer.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Shadow-run compute cost increase. Mitigation: run expensive checks only for PRs that change runtime or model kernels; use sampling for low-risk PRs.
Risk: False positives from streaming diffs due to non-deterministic generation. Mitigation: include semantic-aware tolerance and flag frequency rather than single-session failures.
Risk: SDKs lag behind server changes. Mitigation: add SDK compatibility test jobs and pre-release notes in client package publish pipeline.
